sentences.text:
The present writ petition has been filed seeking following reliefs:
i.

For issuance of an appropriate writ(s)/order(s) and/or direction(s) particularly a writ in the nature of Certiorari for quashing of the Genealogical Table Sl. No.
43/2022 dated 07.03.2022 issued in the name of Birendra Yadav, Genealogical Table Sl. No. 54/2022 dated 22.03.2022 issued in the name of Shankar Yadav,
Genealogical Table Sl. No. 56/2022 dated 23.03.2022 issued in the name of Most.
Lakhpatiya Devi and Genealogical Table Sl. No. 60/2022 dated 30.03.2022 issued in the name of Most. Sugiya (Annexure-11 series), issued by the Circle Officer, Poraiyahat, Dist. Godda on the basis of the applications made by them stating that they are the legal heirs of Late Budhu Mahto that too without verifying any valid documents and also without waiting the outcome/decision of the case registered as R.E.R Case No. 30/2019-20 in the court of Sub-Divisional Officer, Godda which was filed as per the observation made by the Circle Officer, Poraiyahat vide order dated 28.02.2019 in Misc. Case No. 12/2018-19 that the competent court is S.D.O for passing any order in this matter and directed to maintain status quo till the order passed by the competent authority, however,
during pendency of the R.E.R Case No. 30/2019-20, the Circle Officer issued the above Genealogical Tables which is bad in law.

ii. For issuance of an appropriate writ(s)/order(s) and/or direction(s) particularly a writ in the nature of Mandamus commanding upon the respondent no. 5 to delete the name of the persons whose name appeared at Sl. Nos. 123 to 129 in the NHAI Award Raiyat Payment Notice issued vide Land Acquisition Record No. 57/2020-21 dated 30.12.2022 based on submission of false and fabricated Genealogical Table and not to pay the awarded amount to those persons whose name appeared at Sl. Nos. 123 to 129 in the NHAI Award Raiyat Payment Notice dated 30.12.2022 without proper verification and till the decision taken by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Godda (the respondent no. 3) in R.E.R Case No. 30/2019-20.
iii

For issuance of an appropriate writ(s)/order(s) and/or direction(s) particularly a writ in the nature of Mandamus commanding upon the respondent no. 3 to dispose of R.E.R Case No.

sentences.text:
iv For issuance of an appropriate writ(s)/order(s) and/or direction(s) particularly a writ in the nature of Certiorari for quashing the order dated 23.05.2020 (Annexure-9/1) whereby and whereunder the Circle Officer, Poraiyahat has rejected the application of the son of the petitioner no. 1 namely, Baleshwar Yadav who had prayed for cancellation of the Cast Certificate, Residential Certificate, Income Certificate of Ranjit Yadav S/o Mahendra Yadav which was issued by the Circle Officer, Poraiyahat on the basis of false and fabricated genealogical table.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioners is directed to implead the Project Director, National Highways Authority of India, Project Implementation Unit, Deoghar as respondent no. 19 in the present writ petition.
3. Let necessary insertion in the cause title of the writ petition be made by learned counsel for the petitioners in course of the day.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners undertakes to serve a copy of the writ petition to Mr. Amrit Raj Kisku, AC to Mrs. Sweety Topno, learned counsel for the newly impleaded respondent no. 19 (NHAI).
5.

Learned counsel for the State respondents as well as respondent no. 19 jointly raise objection with regard to maintainability of the writ petition on the ground that in fact the petitioners have an efficacious remedy for redressal of the aforesaid grievances under Section 3-H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 by making an application before the respondent no. 5 - the District Land Acquisition Officer, Godda-cum-Competent Authority under the Act, 1956 to get the dispute referred for the decision of the Principal Civil Court of Original Jurisdiction within whose limits the aforesaid lands are situated.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.
7.

The contention of the petitioners that the genealogical certificates have wrongly been issued by the respondent no. 6 - the Circle Officer, Poraiyahat, Godda to the private respondents so as to enable them to receive the awarded amount of compensation in lieu of acquisition of the lands in question.

The said contention is factual in nature which is required to be adjudicated by a competent court under Section 3-H(4) of the Act, 1956 as the said provision provides forum to the concerned persons not only to agitate the issue of apportionment of the amount of compensation, but for adjudication of the dispute as to who would be legally entitled to receive the compensation.

8. Under the said circumstance, without commenting on the merit of the case, the petitioners are given liberty to prefer application(s)/objection invoking Section 3-H(4) of the Act, 1956 before the respondent no. 5.

On receipt of the said application(s)/objection, the respondent no. 5 shall refer the dispute to the decision of the concerned Principal Civil Court of Original Jurisdiction within thirty days from the date of receipt of this order.
